newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Europe's cash cocoa buyers scarce but so is supply.
newsitem.headline: Europe's cash cocoa buyers scarce but so is supply.

text.p: Cash cocoa buyers stayed sidelined this week, with scattered purchases reported from north European industry but physical traders said Ivorian supply was restricted and there were few offers in the market.
"There's been very little offtake, and that's been reflected in the terminal market," one trader said.
London-traded futures have edged higher this week, with the benchmark July position progressing from around 1,030 stg seven days ago to near 1,040 on Thursday.
"It's been just replacement buying and nothing more," another said. "But this market is so dull at the moment."
Traders said the purchases were all nearby material of Ivorian origin at differentials similar to last week when beans were trading at between 15 and 20 stg under the terminal market.
Some said low quality beans were also appearing on the physical market and this had hampered trading volumes.

Others blamed the lack of offers in the market on confusion surrounding the Ivory Coast's cocoa marketing board -- the Caisse de Stabilisation (Caistab), where over-bidding for contracts was still continuing.
In Abidjan, export sources said Ivorian port stocks stood at 150,000 tonnes after busy March exports but some shippers remained short of cocoa for May contracts as arrivals dwindle.

A World Bank delegation was believed to be arriving in the country next week, following up a visit by donors and industry members in February to examine how the privatisation programme was progressing.

Traders reckoned the level of farmer prices, set within the bareme guidelines set up by the Caisse, would have to be raised under pressure from donor bodies. This could further restrict supplies of cocoa coming out of the country in the near future.
"If farmers know they are going to get more money, then they will hold back cocoa and blend it in with new crop," one said.
